theory.title: Exercise 1.3.1: Should Be Equal - The Foundation of Validation
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 brings up two holographic panels side by side, both displaying "OPERATIONAL".

"PROTO-7, storing data is only half the job. We must verify it's correct. The Should Be Equal keyword is your primary validation tool—it compares actual vs expected values."

What Are Assertions?

Assertions are statements that validate expected conditions. If the condition is true, the test continues. If false, the test fails immediately with an error.

Why Assertions Matter

  • Catch bugs early: Test fails when behavior changes unexpectedly
  • Document expectations: Code shows what should happen
  • Prevent regressions: Ensure fixes don't break again
  • Build confidence: Passing tests mean working software

The Should Be Equal Keyword

The most fundamental assertion in Robot Framework:

Should Be Equal    ${actual}    ${expected}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If ${actual} == ${expected} → Test continues
  • ❌ If ${actual} ≠ ${expected} → Test fails with error message

Basic Usage

*** Test Cases ***
Simple Equality Check
    ${status}           Set Variable    Operational
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational
    Log                 Validation passed!

What Happens:

  1. Create variable ${status} with value "Operational"
  2. Compare ${status} to "Operational"
  3. They match → assertion passes → test continues
  4. Log success message

When Assertions Fail

*** Test Cases ***
Failing Assertion Example
    ${status}           Set Variable    Damaged
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational
    # ❌ TEST FAILS HERE - next line never executes
    Log                 This won't run

Error Message:

AssertionError: Damaged != Operational

The test stops at the failed assertion. Subsequent keywords don't execute.

Comparing Variables

*** Test Cases ***
Compare Two Variables
    ${actual}           Set Variable    Robot Framework
    ${expected}         Set Variable    Robot Framework
    Should Be Equal     ${actual}    ${expected}
    Log                 Both variables match!

String Comparison (Default)

By default, Should Be Equal compares values as strings:

*** Test Cases ***
String Comparison
    ${number_as_string}    Set Variable    42
    Should Be Equal        ${number_as_string}    42      # ✅ Works: "42" == "42"
    Should Be Equal        ${number_as_string}    042     # ❌ Fails: "42" != "042"

Adding Custom Error Messages

You can add a custom message as the third argument:

*** Test Cases ***
Custom Error Message
    ${status}    Set Variable    Damaged
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    Operational    msg=System status check failed! Expected Operational but got ${status}

Error Output:

AssertionError: System status check failed! Expected Operational but got Damaged

Common Use Cases

1. API Response Validation

*** Test Cases ***
API Status Check
    ${response_status}    Set Variable    200
    Should Be Equal       ${response_status}    200    msg=Expected HTTP 200 OK

2. Configuration Verification

*** Test Cases ***
Config Check
    ${env}              Set Variable    production
    ${expected_env}     Set Variable    production
    Should Be Equal     ${env}    ${expected_env}    msg=Environment mismatch!

3. User Input Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Login Check
    ${username}         Set Variable    admin@example.com
    Should Be Equal     ${username}    admin@example.com

Should Be Equal vs Should Be Equal As Strings

KeywordBehaviorWhen to Use
Should Be Equal String comparison (default) Most common cases
Should Be Equal As Strings Explicit string comparison When clarity needed
Should Be Equal As Integers Numeric comparison Comparing numbers: 42 == 042
Should Be Equal As Numbers Float/decimal comparison Comparing 3.14 == 3.140

Case Sensitivity

String comparisons ARE case-sensitive:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Matters
    ${status}           Set Variable    operational
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational    # ❌ FAILS: "operational" != "Operational"

Use Should Be Equal As Strings with ignore_case=True for case-insensitive:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Insensitive
    ${status}                      Set Variable    operational
    Should Be Equal As Strings     ${status}    Operational    ignore_case=True    # ✅ PASSES

Assertion Keyword Flexibility

Like all Robot Framework keywords, assertion keywords are case-insensitive and spacing-flexible:

*** Test Cases ***
Keyword Variations
    ${x}    Set Variable    test
    
    Should Be Equal          ${x}    test    # Standard
    should be equal          ${x}    test    # Lowercase
    SHOULD BE EQUAL          ${x}    test    # Uppercase
    Should··Be··Equal        ${x}    test    # Extra spaces
    ShouldBeEqual            ${x}    test    # No spaces
    
    # All are IDENTICAL!

Best Practices

1. Descriptive Variable Names

*** Test Cases ***
Good Practice
    ${actual_status}      Set Variable    OK
    ${expected_status}    Set Variable    OK
    Should Be Equal       ${actual_status}    ${expected_status}
    
    # Clear what's being compared

2. Use Custom Error Messages for Complex Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Errors
    ${user_role}    Set Variable    guest
    Should Be Equal    ${user_role}    admin    msg=User does not have admin privileges (role: ${user_role})

3. One Assertion Per Logical Check

*** Test Cases ***
Multiple Checks
    ${status}    Set Variable    active
    ${role}      Set Variable    admin
    
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    active    msg=Status check failed
    Should Be Equal    ${role}      admin     msg=Role check failed
    
    # Separate assertions = separate failure messages

Common Mistakes

❌ Wrong: Comparing without storing

*** Test Cases ***
Wrong Approach
    Should Be Equal    Operational    Operational    # Works but no actual value tested

✅ Right: Store actual value first

*** Test Cases ***
Correct Approach
    ${status}           Set Variable    Operational
    Should Be Equal     ${status}    Operational

MENTOR-9: "Create two variables: one for actual ship status, one for expected. Use Should Be Equal to validate they match. Then verify the ship name. Show me you can catch discrepancies before they become disasters."

theory.title: Exercise 1.3.2: Should Contain - Flexible String Validation
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 displays a holographic error message with specific words highlighted.

"PROTO-7, exact matches aren't always practical. Error messages have timestamps, IDs, variable data. The Should Contain keyword lets you verify the important parts while ignoring the rest."

What is Should Contain?

Should Contain validates that a string contains a specific substring. It's a partial match assertion.

Why Partial Matching Matters

  • Error messages: "Error at 14:23:47 - Hull breach detected" contains "breach"
  • Dynamic content: "User #1234 logged in successfully" contains "logged in"
  • Flexible validation: Don't care about exact format, just key information
  • Real-world data: Timestamps, IDs, and variable parts change constantly

Basic Syntax

Should Contain    ${string}    ${substring}

Arguments:

  • First argument: The full string to search in
  • Second argument: The substring to find

Simple Example

*** Test Cases ***
Error Message Check
    ${error}           Set Variable    Hull breach detected in sector 7
    Should Contain     ${error}    breach
    Log                Error contains 'breach' - validation passed!

What Happens:

  1. Create variable with full error message
  2. Check if "breach" exists anywhere in the message
  3. ✅ Found → assertion passes
  4. Log success

Case Sensitivity

Important: Should Contain is case-sensitive by default!

*** Test Cases ***
Case Sensitive Search
    ${message}         Set Variable    Hull Breach detected
    Should Contain     ${message}    Breach     # ✅ PASSES - exact case match
    Should Contain     ${message}    breach     # ❌ FAILS - case mismatch

For case-insensitive matching, convert to same case first:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Insensitive Check
    ${message}         Set Variable    Hull Breach Detected
    ${lower_msg}       Convert To Lowercase    ${message}
    Should Contain     ${lower_msg}    breach    # ✅ PASSES

Multiple Substring Checks

You can verify multiple substrings in the same message:

*** Test Cases ***
Multi-Check Validation
    ${report}          Set Variable    Diagnostic: 3 warnings, 1 critical error
    Should Contain     ${report}    warnings
    Should Contain     ${report}    critical
    Should Contain     ${report}    error
    Log                All key terms found!

Real-World Use Cases

1. Error Log Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Check Error Logs
    ${log_entry}       Set Variable    [2157-03-15 14:23:47] ERROR: Connection timeout - retry failed
    Should Contain     ${log_entry}    ERROR
    Should Contain     ${log_entry}    timeout
    Should Contain     ${log_entry}    retry failed

2. API Response Validation

*** Test Cases ***
API Response Check
    ${response}        Set Variable    {"status": "success", "user_id": 1234, "message": "Login successful"}
    Should Contain     ${response}    success
    Should Contain     ${response}    user_id

3. Page Content Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Web Page Validation
    ${page_content}    Set Variable    Welcome to Starlight Explorer Dashboard
    Should Contain     ${page_content}    Welcome
    Should Contain     ${page_content}    Dashboard

Should Contain vs Should Be Equal

AspectShould Be EqualShould Contain
Match Type Exact match Partial match (substring)
When to Use Values must be identical Only care about key parts
Flexibility Strict Flexible
Example "Error" == "Error" "Error at 14:23" contains "Error"

Custom Error Messages

*** Test Cases ***
Custom Message
    ${status}    Set Variable    System operational - no errors
    Should Contain    ${status}    error    msg=Status message should contain 'error' keyword

Failure Output:

AssertionError: Status message should contain 'error' keyword

Related Keywords

Should Not Contain

Verifies a string does NOT contain a substring:

*** Test Cases ***
Negative Check
    ${status}              Set Variable    System operational
    Should Not Contain     ${status}    error    # ✅ PASSES - no 'error' found

Should Contain X Times

Verifies exact number of occurrences:

*** Test Cases ***
Count Occurrences
    ${log}                      Set Variable    ERROR: failed, ERROR: timeout, ERROR: disconnect
    Should Contain X Times      ${log}    ERROR    3

Best Practices

1. Choose Meaningful Substrings

*** Test Cases ***
Good Substring Choice
    ${error}    Set Variable    Critical hull breach in sector 7 - immediate action required

    # ✅ Good: Specific key term
    Should Contain    ${error}    breach

    # ❌ Bad: Too generic
    Should Contain    ${error}    in

2. Be Careful with Case

*** Test Cases ***
Case Awareness
    ${msg}    Set Variable    ERROR: System Failure

    # Know your data's case!
    Should Contain    ${msg}    ERROR     # ✅ PASSES
    Should Contain    ${msg}    error     # ❌ FAILS

3. Combine with Other Assertions

*** Test Cases ***
Combined Validation
    ${response}    Set Variable    {"status": "error", "code": 500}

    Should Contain     ${response}    error          # Has error
    Should Contain     ${response}    500            # Has status code
    Length Should Be   ${response}    35             # Correct length

MENTOR-9: "Create an error message with dynamic parts. Use Should Contain to verify it includes 'breach' and 'sector 7'. Then check a status report for 'critical error'. Show me you can extract meaning from messy real-world data."

exercises.title: Should Be True/False - Boolean Validation
exercises.description: Learn to validate boolean conditions and logical expressions.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Sometimes you need to evaluate conditions—is the temperature safe? Are repairs complete? Boolean assertions handle this."
story.context: Boolean validations check if conditions are True or False. Essential for conditional logic verification.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent! You verified that 5 > 3 is True. Boolean logic is the foundation of intelligent testing."

Use Should Be True with expression: ${temp} < ${max_temp}
Use Should Be True to verify ${repairs_done}
Use Should Be False to verify ${system_offline}

Should Be False syntax: Should Be False    ${condition}
Expressions: ${x} > ${y}, ${x} < ${y}, ${x} == ${y}

Expressions are evaluated as Python expressions
Use quotes for string comparisons: '${x}' == 'value'

theory.title: Exercise 1.3.3: Should Be True/False - Boolean Logic
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 projects three holographic logic gates, each showing different boolean evaluations.

"PROTO-7, not all validations compare values. Sometimes you need to evaluate conditions—is the temperature safe? Are repairs complete? The Should Be True and Should Be False keywords handle boolean logic."

What are Boolean Assertions?

Boolean assertions validate that conditions evaluate to True or False. They're essential for:

  • Conditional checks: Is temperature below maximum?
  • State validation: Are repairs complete?
  • Logical expressions: Is count greater than threshold?
  • Flag verification: Is system online?

Should Be True

Validates that a condition or expression evaluates to True:

Should Be True    ${condition}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If condition is True → assertion passes
  • ❌ If condition is False → test fails

Should Be False

Validates that a condition or expression evaluates to False:

Should Be False    ${condition}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If condition is False → assertion passes
  • ❌ If condition is True → test fails

Boolean Constants

Robot Framework provides boolean constants:

*** Test Cases ***
Boolean Constants
    ${flag1}           Set Variable    ${True}      # Boolean True
    ${flag2}           Set Variable    ${False}     # Boolean False
    Should Be True     ${flag1}                     # ✅ PASSES
    Should Be False    ${flag2}                     # ✅ PASSES

Important: ${True} and ${False} are special Robot Framework variables (note the capital T and F).

Evaluating Expressions

The real power comes from evaluating Python-style expressions:

*** Test Cases ***
Expression Evaluation
    ${temp}            Set Variable    45
    ${max_temp}        Set Variable    50

    # Evaluate: is 45 < 50?
    Should Be True     ${temp} < ${max_temp}        # ✅ PASSES

Comparison Operators

OperatorMeaningExample
< Less than ${temp} < ${max}
> Greater than ${count} > ${min}
== Equal to ${status} == 'OK'
!= Not equal to ${error} != 'None'
<= Less than or equal ${value} <= 100
>= Greater than or equal ${score} >= 75

Numeric Comparisons

*** Test Cases ***
Temperature Check
    ${current_temp}    Set Variable    75
    ${max_safe}        Set Variable    100
    ${min_safe}        Set Variable    0

    Should Be True     ${current_temp} < ${max_safe}     # Below max
    Should Be True     ${current_temp} > ${min_safe}     # Above min
    Log                Temperature within safe range!

String Comparisons

For string comparisons, use quotes around the expected value:

*** Test Cases ***
Status Check
    ${status}          Set Variable    operational

    # String comparison - need quotes!
    Should Be True     '${status}' == 'operational'      # ✅ PASSES
    Should Be False    '${status}' == 'offline'          # ✅ PASSES

Logical Operators

Combine conditions with and, or, not:

*** Test Cases ***
Combined Conditions
    ${temp}            Set Variable    75
    ${pressure}        Set Variable    850

    # AND: both must be true
    Should Be True     ${temp} < 100 and ${pressure} < 1000

    # OR: at least one must be true
    Should Be True     ${temp} > 80 or ${pressure} > 900

    # NOT: negates condition
    Should Be True     not ${temp} > 100

Real-World Use Cases

1. Safety Threshold Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Safety Check
    ${radiation_level}    Set Variable    45
    ${safe_limit}         Set Variable    50

    Should Be True        ${radiation_level} < ${safe_limit}
    Log                   Radiation within safe limits

2. Status Flag Verification

*** Test Cases ***
System Status
    ${repairs_complete}    Set Variable    ${True}
    ${system_damaged}      Set Variable    ${False}

    Should Be True         ${repairs_complete}
    Should Be False        ${system_damaged}
    Log                    All systems operational

3. Range Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Value Range Check
    ${power_level}     Set Variable    65

    # Value must be between 50 and 100
    Should Be True     ${power_level} >= 50 and ${power_level} <= 100
    Log                Power level within operational range

Error Messages

When boolean assertions fail, the error shows the evaluated expression:

*** Test Cases ***
Failed Boolean Check
    ${temp}            Set Variable    110
    ${max}             Set Variable    100

    Should Be True     ${temp} < ${max}
    # ❌ ERROR: 110 < 100 should be true but was not

Custom Error Messages

Add custom messages for clarity:

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Message
    ${damage_count}    Set Variable    5
    ${max_allowed}     Set Variable    3

    Should Be True     ${damage_count} <= ${max_allowed}
    ...                msg=Damage count ${damage_count} exceeds maximum ${max_allowed}!

Failure Output:

AssertionError: Damage count 5 exceeds maximum 3!

Should Be True vs Numeric Assertions

AspectShould Be TrueShould Be Greater/Less Than
Syntax Should Be True ${x} < ${y} Should Be Less Than ${x} ${y}
Flexibility Any boolean expression Only comparisons
When to Use Complex conditions, logical operators Simple numeric comparisons
Example ${x} < ${y} and ${z} > 0 Compare two numbers

Advanced: Variable Type Checking

*** Test Cases ***
Type Validation
    ${value}           Set Variable    ${True}
    ${number}          Set Variable    42

    # Check if variable is boolean True
    Should Be True     ${value} is ${True}

    # Check if value is numeric
    Should Be True     isinstance(${number}, int)

Best Practices

1. Use Quotes for String Comparisons

*** Test Cases ***
String Comparison
    ${status}    Set Variable    OK

    # ✅ Correct: Quotes around strings
    Should Be True    '${status}' == 'OK'

    # ❌ Wrong: Without quotes may cause errors
    Should Be True    ${status} == OK

2. Simplify When Possible

*** Test Cases ***
Simplification
    ${flag}    Set Variable    ${True}

    # ❌ Redundant
    Should Be True    ${flag} == ${True}

    # ✅ Simpler
    Should Be True    ${flag}

3. Combine Related Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Combined Checks
    ${temp}        Set Variable    75
    ${pressure}    Set Variable    900

    # ✅ Good: One assertion for related conditions
    Should Be True    ${temp} < 100 and ${pressure} < 1000

    # Less efficient: Separate assertions
    Should Be True    ${temp} < 100
    Should Be True    ${pressure} < 1000

MENTOR-9: "Validate temperature and repair status. Create ${temp}=45, ${max_temp}=50, and verify temp is below max. Then create ${repairs_done}=${True} and validate it. Finally, create ${system_offline}=${False} and verify it's False. Show me you understand boolean logic."

theory.title: Exercise 1.3.4: Numeric Comparisons
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 activates two holographic gauge displays showing critical ship systems.

"PROTO-7, sometimes you need to verify values are within safe ranges—temperature below maximum, damage count above threshold. Robot Framework provides dedicated keywords for numeric comparisons."

What are Numeric Comparison Keywords?

Numeric comparison keywords validate relationships between numbers. They're essential for:

  • Threshold validation: Is temperature below danger zone?
  • Range checking: Is value within acceptable limits?
  • Performance metrics: Is response time under maximum?
  • Resource monitoring: Is memory usage above minimum?

Should Be Greater Than

Validates that a number is greater than another:

Should Be Greater Than    ${value}    ${minimum}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If value > minimum → assertion passes
  • ❌ If value ≤ minimum → test fails

Should Be Less Than

Validates that a number is less than another:

Should Be Less Than    ${value}    ${maximum}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If value < maximum → assertion passes
  • ❌ If value ≥ maximum → test fails

Basic Examples

*** Test Cases ***
Temperature Check
    ${temp}            Set Variable    75
    ${max_temp}        Set Variable    100

    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${max_temp}    # ✅ PASSES
    Log                    Temperature within safe limits
*** Test Cases ***
Damage Assessment
    ${damage_count}    Set Variable    5
    ${min_repairs}     Set Variable    3

    Should Be Greater Than    ${damage_count}    ${min_repairs}    # ✅ PASSES
    Log                       Repairs needed!

Complete Comparison Keyword Set

KeywordTest Passes WhenExample
Should Be Greater Than value > minimum 5 > 3 ✅
Should Be Less Than value < maximum 75 < 100 ✅
Should Be Greater Than Or Equal To value ≥ minimum 5 ≥ 5 ✅
Should Be Less Than Or Equal To value ≤ maximum 100 ≤ 100 ✅

Range Validation

Combine comparisons to validate values within a range:

*** Test Cases ***
Safe Operating Range
    ${power_level}     Set Variable    65
    ${min_power}       Set Variable    50
    ${max_power}       Set Variable    100

    # Value must be BETWEEN min and max
    Should Be Greater Than    ${power_level}    ${min_power}     # 65 > 50 ✅
    Should Be Less Than       ${power_level}    ${max_power}     # 65 < 100 ✅
    Log                       Power level within safe range

Number Types

These keywords work with both integers and floating-point numbers:

*** Test Cases ***
Integer and Float Comparisons
    ${int_value}       Set Variable    42
    ${float_value}     Set Variable    3.14

    Should Be Greater Than    ${int_value}      40        # Integers
    Should Be Less Than       ${float_value}    4.0       # Floats
    Should Be Greater Than    ${float_value}    ${int_value}    # Mixed ❌ 3.14 not > 42

Real-World Use Cases

1. System Temperature Monitoring

*** Test Cases ***
Engine Temperature Check
    ${engine_temp}     Set Variable    85
    ${max_safe}        Set Variable    100

    Should Be Less Than    ${engine_temp}    ${max_safe}
    Log                    Engine temperature safe (${engine_temp}°C)

2. Resource Threshold Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Memory Usage Check
    ${used_memory}     Set Variable    4096
    ${min_required}    Set Variable    2048

    Should Be Greater Than    ${used_memory}    ${min_required}
    Log                       Sufficient memory available

3. Performance Metrics

*** Test Cases ***
Response Time Validation
    ${response_ms}     Set Variable    250
    ${max_allowed}     Set Variable    500

    Should Be Less Than    ${response_ms}    ${max_allowed}
    Log                    Response time acceptable (${response_ms}ms)

Error Messages

When comparisons fail, you get clear error messages:

*** Test Cases ***
Failed Comparison
    ${temp}            Set Variable    110
    ${max}             Set Variable    100

    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${max}
    # ❌ ERROR: 110 should be less than 100

Custom Error Messages

Add custom messages for better debugging:

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Message
    ${radiation}       Set Variable    55
    ${safe_limit}      Set Variable    50

    Should Be Less Than    ${radiation}    ${safe_limit}
    ...                    msg=Radiation level ${radiation} exceeds safe limit ${safe_limit}!

Failure Output:

AssertionError: Radiation level 55 exceeds safe limit 50!

Numeric vs Boolean Comparisons

AspectNumeric KeywordsShould Be True
Syntax Should Be Less Than ${x} ${y} Should Be True ${x} < ${y}
Readability More explicit, easier to read More compact, Pythonic
Error Messages "42 should be less than 100" "42 < 100 should be true"
When to Use Simple numeric comparisons Complex conditions, multiple checks

Equivalent Comparisons

*** Test Cases ***
Same Validation - Different Approaches
    ${value}           Set Variable    75
    ${max}             Set Variable    100

    # Approach 1: Numeric keyword (clearer)
    Should Be Less Than    ${value}    ${max}

    # Approach 2: Boolean expression (more flexible)
    Should Be True         ${value} < ${max}

Precision with Floats

Floating-point comparisons work but be aware of precision issues:

*** Test Cases ***
Float Precision
    ${pi}              Set Variable    3.14159
    ${approx_pi}       Set Variable    3.14

    Should Be Greater Than    ${pi}    ${approx_pi}    # ✅ 3.14159 > 3.14

    # For precise float comparisons, consider tolerance
    ${difference}      Evaluate    abs(${pi} - 3.14159)
    Should Be Less Than    ${difference}    0.00001

Negative Numbers

Numeric keywords handle negative numbers correctly:

*** Test Cases ***
Negative Number Comparison
    ${temp}            Set Variable    -15
    ${freezing}        Set Variable    0

    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${freezing}    # ✅ -15 < 0

Best Practices

1. Use Descriptive Variable Names

*** Test Cases ***
Descriptive Names
    # ✅ Good: Clear intent
    ${current_temp}    Set Variable    75
    ${max_safe_temp}   Set Variable    100
    Should Be Less Than    ${current_temp}    ${max_safe_temp}

    # ❌ Less clear
    ${a}               Set Variable    75
    ${b}               Set Variable    100
    Should Be Less Than    ${a}    ${b}

2. Add Context with Logging

*** Test Cases ***
Contextual Logging
    ${damage}          Set Variable    7
    ${threshold}       Set Variable    5

    Should Be Greater Than    ${damage}    ${threshold}
    Log                       Damage count (${damage}) exceeds threshold (${threshold}) - repairs required

3. Combine with Custom Messages

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Messages
    ${score}           Set Variable    45
    ${passing}         Set Variable    60

    Should Be Greater Than    ${score}    ${passing}
    ...                       msg=Score ${score} below passing grade ${passing}

4. Validate Both Boundaries for Ranges

*** Test Cases ***
Range Validation
    ${value}           Set Variable    75

    # ✅ Good: Validate both min and max
    Should Be Greater Than    ${value}    50
    Should Be Less Than       ${value}    100

    # ✅ Alternative: Use >= and <= if boundaries are inclusive
    Should Be Greater Than Or Equal To    ${value}    50
    Should Be Less Than Or Equal To       ${value}    100

MENTOR-9: "Validate ship systems. Create ${reactor_temp}=85, ${max_temp}=100, verify temp below max. Then create ${hull_damage}=7, ${repair_threshold}=5, verify damage above threshold. Finally, create ${power}=65 and validate it's between 50 and 100. Show me you understand numeric validation."

theory.title: Exercise 1.3.5: Length Validations
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 projects holographic displays showing various data collections—lists of systems, error codes, and repair queues.

"PROTO-7, collections have size constraints. You need to verify the number of items in lists, the character count in strings, or ensure containers are empty. These validations ensure data integrity."

What are Length Validation Keywords?

Length validation keywords check the size of collections and strings. They're essential for:

  • Collection size: Does the list have exactly 5 items?
  • String length: Is the error code 10 characters?
  • Empty checks: Is the queue empty?
  • Capacity validation: Are there enough resources?

Length Should Be

Validates that a collection or string has an exact length:

Length Should Be    ${item}    ${expected_length}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If actual length == expected → assertion passes
  • ❌ If lengths don't match → test fails

Works with:

  • Lists
  • Dictionaries
  • Strings
  • Tuples
  • Sets

Should Be Empty

Validates that a collection or string is empty (length = 0):

Should Be Empty    ${item}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If length == 0 → assertion passes
  • ❌ If length > 0 → test fails

Should Not Be Empty

Validates that a collection or string has at least one item:

Should Not Be Empty    ${item}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If length > 0 → assertion passes
  • ❌ If length == 0 → test fails

List Length Validation

*** Test Cases ***
System Count Check
    @{systems}         Create List    Navigation    Power    Life Support    Comms    Sensors

    Length Should Be    ${systems}    5    # ✅ PASSES - list has 5 items
    Log                 All 5 critical systems detected

String Length Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Error Code Format Check
    ${error_code}      Set Variable    ERR-2157-03-15-HULL

    Length Should Be    ${error_code}    19    # ✅ PASSES - 19 characters
    Log                 Error code format valid

Empty Collection Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Repair Queue Status
    @{pending_repairs}    Create List    # Empty list

    Should Be Empty    ${pending_repairs}    # ✅ PASSES - no items
    Log                No pending repairs - all systems operational

Non-Empty Collection Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Active Errors Check
    @{active_errors}    Create List    Hull breach    Power failure

    Should Not Be Empty    ${active_errors}    # ✅ PASSES - has items
    Log                    ${active_errors.__len__()} errors detected

Dictionary Length Validation

For dictionaries, length is the number of keys:

*** Test Cases ***
System Status Count
    &{status}          Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE    Power=CRITICAL    Life_Support=OK

    Length Should Be    ${status}    3    # ✅ PASSES - 3 keys
    Log                 Monitoring 3 systems

Real-World Use Cases

1. Resource Availability

*** Test Cases ***
Available Tools Check
    @{tools}           Create List    Wrench    Welder    Scanner    Diagnostic Tablet

    Length Should Be    ${tools}    4
    Log                 All 4 required tools available

2. Data Format Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Serial Number Format
    ${serial}          Set Variable    SN-7734-PROTO

    Length Should Be    ${serial}    13    # Must be exactly 13 characters
    Log                 Serial number format valid

3. Queue Processing

*** Test Cases ***
Message Queue Empty After Processing
    @{messages}        Create List    # Simulate processed queue

    Should Be Empty    ${messages}
    Log                All messages processed successfully

4. Batch Size Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Repair Batch Size
    @{repairs}         Create List    Hull    Engine    Sensors

    Should Not Be Empty    ${repairs}               # Has items
    Length Should Be       ${repairs}    3          # Exactly 3 repairs
    Log                    Processing batch of 3 repairs

Error Messages

When length validations fail, you get specific error messages:

*** Test Cases ***
Failed Length Check
    @{systems}         Create List    Nav    Power    Life Support

    Length Should Be    ${systems}    5
    # ❌ ERROR: Length of list should be 5 but is 3

Custom Error Messages

Add custom messages for clarity:

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Message
    @{crew}            Create List    PROTO-7    MENTOR-9

    Length Should Be    ${crew}    4
    ...                 msg=Expected 4 crew members but found ${crew.__len__()}

Failure Output:

AssertionError: Expected 4 crew members but found 2

Getting Length Programmatically

Robot Framework provides the Get Length keyword:

*** Test Cases ***
Dynamic Length Check
    @{systems}         Create List    Nav    Power    Comms
    ${count}           Get Length    ${systems}

    Log                 Found ${count} systems
    Should Be True      ${count} > 2    # At least 3 systems

Combining Length with Other Validations

*** Test Cases ***
Complete Validation
    @{errors}          Create List    ERR-001    ERR-002    ERR-003

    # Check we have errors
    Should Not Be Empty    ${errors}

    # Check we don't have too many
    ${error_count}     Get Length    ${errors}
    Should Be Less Than    ${error_count}    10    # Max 10 errors

    # Check exact count
    Length Should Be    ${errors}    3

Empty String vs Empty List

Both strings and lists can be empty:

*** Test Cases ***
Empty Validations
    ${empty_string}    Set Variable    ${EMPTY}
    @{empty_list}      Create List

    Should Be Empty    ${empty_string}    # ✅ Empty string
    Should Be Empty    ${empty_list}      # ✅ Empty list

    Length Should Be    ${empty_string}    0
    Length Should Be    ${empty_list}      0

Built-in ${EMPTY} Variable

Robot Framework provides the ${EMPTY} constant for empty strings:

*** Test Cases ***
Empty Variable
    ${name}            Set Variable    ${EMPTY}

    Should Be Empty    ${name}
    Should Be Equal    ${name}    ${EMPTY}
    Length Should Be    ${name}    0

Best Practices

1. Use Length Should Be for Exact Counts

*** Test Cases ***
Exact Count
    @{systems}         Create List    A    B    C    D    E

    # ✅ Good: Exact expected count
    Length Should Be    ${systems}    5

    # ❌ Less precise
    Should Be True      ${systems.__len__()} == 5

2. Use Should Be Empty for Clarity

*** Test Cases ***
Empty Check
    @{queue}           Create List

    # ✅ Good: Intent is clear
    Should Be Empty    ${queue}

    # ✅ Also valid but less readable
    Length Should Be    ${queue}    0

3. Validate Before Processing

*** Test Cases ***
Safe Processing
    @{repairs}         Create List    Hull    Engine

    # Ensure we have items before processing
    Should Not Be Empty    ${repairs}
    Log                    Processing ${repairs.__len__()} repairs...

4. Use Get Length for Dynamic Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Dynamic Validation
    @{errors}          Create List    ERR-1    ERR-2    ERR-3
    ${count}           Get Length    ${errors}

    Log                 Error count: ${count}
    Should Be True      ${count} >= 1 and ${count} <= 10    # Between 1 and 10

Common Patterns

PatternUse CaseExample
Length Should Be Exact count required Password must be 8 characters
Should Be Empty Verify queue/list cleared All tasks completed
Should Not Be Empty Ensure data exists Search returned results
Get Length + comparisons Range validation Between 1 and 100 items

Advanced: Nested Collection Lengths

*** Test Cases ***
Nested Collection Validation
    @{system_groups}    Create List
    ...                 ${EMPTY}    # Group 1: empty
    ...                 ${EMPTY}    # Group 2: empty

    # Outer list has 2 groups
    Length Should Be    ${system_groups}    2

    # Each group is empty
    Should Be Empty     ${system_groups}[0]
    Should Be Empty     ${system_groups}[1]

MENTOR-9: "Validate ship data structures. Create a list ${critical_systems} with exactly 5 system names. Create an error code ${error} with exactly 19 characters. Create an empty list ${completed_repairs}. Verify all three conditions. Show me you understand length validation."

Assertion Flexibility

theory.title: Exercise 1.3.6: Assertion Flexibility
theory.content:
PROTO-7 looks confused as MENTOR-9 displays the same keyword written five different ways.

"MENTOR-9, these keywords look different—uppercase, lowercase, extra spaces... but they all work?"

MENTOR-9 nods. "Exactly! Robot Framework's keyword flexibility makes writing tests more natural. Keywords are case-insensitive and space-insensitive. This is intentional design."

What is Keyword Flexibility?

Robot Framework keywords follow these rules:

  • Case-insensitive: UPPER, lower, or MiXeD case—all identical
  • Space-insensitive: Underscores, spaces, or no spaces—all identical
  • Whitespace-insensitive: Multiple spaces treated as one
  • Hyphen-insensitive: Hyphens and underscores are interchangeable

Why? This makes keywords more readable and forgiving. You can write in a style that feels natural to you.

Case Insensitivity

All these are identical:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Variations
    ${status}          Set Variable    operational

    Should Be Equal    ${status}    operational    # Standard case
    should be equal    ${status}    operational    # Lowercase
    SHOULD BE EQUAL    ${status}    operational    # Uppercase
    sHoUlD bE eQuAl    ${status}    operational    # Mixed case

    # All four assertions ✅ PASS - they're identical!

Space Insensitivity

Spaces, underscores, and extra whitespace are all treated the same:

*** Test Cases ***
Space Variations
    ${status}          Set Variable    OK

    Should Be Equal    ${status}    OK    # Standard spacing
    Should··Be··Equal  ${status}    OK    # Extra spaces (shown as ··)
    ShouldBeEqual      ${status}    OK    # No spaces
    Should_Be_Equal    ${status}    OK    # Underscores instead

    # All four assertions ✅ PASS - they're identical!

Note: In the example above, ·· represents extra spaces for visibility. In actual code, any amount of whitespace works.

Combined Flexibility

You can mix case and spacing variations:

*** Test Cases ***
Maximum Flexibility
    ${value}           Set Variable    42

    Should Be Equal       ${value}    42
    should_be_equal       ${value}    42
    SHOULDBEEQUAL         ${value}    42
    ShoULD··bE··EQuaL     ${value}    42

    # All ✅ PASS - Robot Framework normalizes them all!

How Normalization Works

Robot Framework internally normalizes all keywords by:

  1. Converting to lowercase
  2. Removing all spaces, underscores, and hyphens
  3. Comparing the result

Examples:

Original KeywordNormalized Form
Should Be Equal shouldbeequal
SHOULD BE EQUAL shouldbeequal
should_be_equal shouldbeequal
ShouldBeEqual shouldbeequal
Should··Be··Equal shouldbeequal

All normalize to shouldbeequal, so they're all identical!

Common Naming Conventions

While any style works, the Robot Framework community uses these conventions:

*** Test Cases ***
Community Conventions

    # ✅ RECOMMENDED: Capitalized with spaces (most readable)
    Should Be Equal       ${value}    expected

    # ✅ COMMON: Lowercase with underscores (Python style)
    should_be_equal       ${value}    expected

    # ✅ ACCEPTABLE: CamelCase (compact)
    ShouldBeEqual         ${value}    expected

    # ❌ UNCOMMON: All uppercase (less readable)
    SHOULD BE EQUAL       ${value}    expected

Best Practice: Choose one style and be consistent within your test suite.

Real-World Examples

1. Team Style Preference

*** Test Cases ***
Team A Style (Capitalized with Spaces)
    ${result}          Set Variable    PASS
    Should Be Equal    ${result}    PASS
    Length Should Be   ${result}    4

Team B Style (Lowercase with Underscores)
    ${result}          Set Variable    PASS
    should_be_equal    ${result}    PASS
    length_should_be   ${result}    4

# Both styles are ✅ VALID - choose what your team prefers

2. Library Keyword Flexibility

This flexibility applies to ALL keywords, including library keywords:

*** Test Cases ***
Library Keyword Variations
    ${text}            Set Variable    Hello Robot Framework

    # All these are identical:
    Log                ${text}
    log                ${text}
    LOG                ${text}
    Log To Console     ${text}
    log_to_console     ${text}
    LOGTOCONSOLE       ${text}

When Flexibility Matters

1. Reading Existing Tests

You might encounter different styles in legacy code—they all work the same:

*** Test Cases ***
Legacy Code Examples
    # Old test from 2015 (uppercase style)
    SHOULD BE EQUAL    ${status}    OK

    # Test from 2018 (underscore style)
    should_be_equal    ${status}    OK

    # Modern test from 2024 (standard style)
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    OK

    # All three ✅ work identically!

2. Natural Language Tests

Flexibility makes tests more readable as sentences:

*** Test Cases ***
Readable Test
    ${temp}            Set Variable    75

    # Reads like English
    Temperature Should Be Less Than Maximum
    # This is a custom keyword, but flexibility applies!

Important: Arguments ARE Case-Sensitive

⚠️ Keyword flexibility does NOT apply to arguments:

*** Test Cases ***
Argument Sensitivity
    ${status}          Set Variable    OPERATIONAL

    # ✅ PASSES - exact match
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    OPERATIONAL

    # ❌ FAILS - arguments are case-sensitive!
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    operational

    # Keywords are flexible, but data must match exactly

Variable Names ARE Case-Sensitive

⚠️ Variable names must match exactly:

*** Test Cases ***
Variable Sensitivity
    ${status}          Set Variable    OK
    ${STATUS}          Set Variable    CRITICAL    # Different variable!

    Should Be Equal    ${status}     OK          # ✅ Uses lowercase variable
    Should Be Equal    ${STATUS}     CRITICAL    # ✅ Uses uppercase variable
    Should Be Equal    ${Status}     ???         # ❌ UNDEFINED - exact match required!

Test Case Names ARE Case-Sensitive

⚠️ Test case names must match exactly when referenced:

*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    Log    Logging in...

LOGIN TEST
    Log    This is a DIFFERENT test case!

# These are two separate test cases!

Hyphens and Underscores

Hyphens (-) and underscores (_) are treated identically in keywords:

*** Test Cases ***
Hyphen vs Underscore
    ${value}           Set Variable    42

    Should-Be-Equal    ${value}    42    # Hyphens
    Should_Be_Equal    ${value}    42    # Underscores
    Should Be Equal    ${value}    42    # Spaces

    # All three ✅ identical!

Best Practices

1. Consistency Within Test Suite

*** Test Cases ***
Consistent Style
    ${status}          Set Variable    OK

    # ✅ Good: Pick one style and stick to it
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    OK
    Should Contain     ${status}    O
    Should Not Be Empty    ${status}

    # ❌ Inconsistent: Mixing styles
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    OK
    should_contain     ${status}    O
    SHOULDNOTBEEMPTY   ${status}

2. Match Your Team's Convention

Follow your project's style guide:

  • Robot Framework official docs: Capitalized With Spaces
  • Python-style teams: lowercase_with_underscores
  • Compact style teams: CamelCase

3. Use Flexibility When Reading, Not Writing

Flexibility helps you understand existing tests, but when writing new tests, stick to one style.

Why This Matters

Keyword flexibility exists because:

  1. Accessibility: Different teams have different conventions
  2. Readability: Tests should read like natural language
  3. Migration: Easier to integrate tests from different sources
  4. Typo-tolerance: Small formatting mistakes don't break tests

Summary Table

AspectFlexible?Example
Keyword names ✅ Yes Should Be Equal = should_be_equal
Keyword spacing ✅ Yes ShouldBeEqual = Should Be Equal
Keyword case ✅ Yes LOG = Log = log
Arguments ❌ No OK ≠ ok
Variable names ❌ No ${status} ≠ ${STATUS}
Test case names ❌ No Login Test ≠ LOGIN TEST

Advanced: Custom Keyword Flexibility

When you create custom keywords, they inherit the same flexibility:

*** Keywords ***
Validate System Status
    [Arguments]    ${system}    ${expected}
    ${status}      Get System Status    ${system}
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    ${expected}

*** Test Cases ***
Custom Keyword Variations
    # All these call the same keyword:
    Validate System Status    Navigation    OFFLINE
    validate_system_status    Navigation    OFFLINE
    VALIDATESYSTEMSTATUS      Navigation    OFFLINE

    # ✅ All work identically!

MENTOR-9: "Demonstrate keyword flexibility. Write a test case that uses Should Be Equal with THREE different naming styles: (1) standard capitalized with spaces, (2) all lowercase with underscores, (3) all uppercase. All should validate ${status}=operational. Show me you understand this is the SAME keyword."

theory.title: Exercise 1.3.7: Collection Assertions
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 projects two holographic data structures—a list of damaged systems and a dictionary of system statuses.

"PROTO-7, you'll often work with collections—lists of components, dictionaries of settings. You need keywords to verify what's inside them. Let me show you collection-specific assertions."

What are Collection Assertion Keywords?

Collection assertion keywords validate the contents of lists and dictionaries. They're essential for:

  • Membership checks: Is "Navigation" in the damaged systems list?
  • Key validation: Does the config dictionary have a "timeout" setting?
  • Value verification: Does the list contain expected items?
  • Configuration testing: Are required keys present?

List Should Contain Value

Validates that a list contains a specific value:

List Should Contain Value    ${list}    ${expected_value}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If value is in list → assertion passes
  • ❌ If value not found → test fails

Dictionary Should Contain Key

Validates that a dictionary contains a specific key:

Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${dict}    ${expected_key}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If key exists in dictionary → assertion passes
  • ❌ If key not found → test fails

List Value Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Damaged Systems Check
    @{damaged}         Create List    Navigation    Power    Life Support

    List Should Contain Value    ${damaged}    Navigation    # ✅ PASSES
    List Should Contain Value    ${damaged}    Power         # ✅ PASSES
    Log                          Critical systems identified

Dictionary Key Validation

*** Test Cases ***
System Status Keys
    &{status}          Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE    Power=CRITICAL    Life_Support=OK

    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Navigation      # ✅ PASSES
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Power           # ✅ PASSES
    Log                              All required status keys present

Additional Collection Keywords

Dictionary Should Contain Value

Check if a dictionary contains a specific value (not key):

*** Test Cases ***
Status Value Check
    &{status}          Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE    Power=OFFLINE

    Dictionary Should Contain Value    ${status}    OFFLINE    # ✅ PASSES
    Log                                At least one system offline

Dictionary Should Contain Item

Check if a dictionary contains a specific key-value pair:

*** Test Cases ***
Exact Key-Value Check
    &{config}          Create Dictionary    timeout=30    retries=3

    Dictionary Should Contain Item    ${config}    timeout    30    # ✅ PASSES
    Log                               Timeout configuration verified

Real-World Use Cases

1. Damaged Systems Tracking

*** Test Cases ***
Identify Critical Damage
    @{damaged_systems}    Create List    Navigation    Power    Communications

    List Should Contain Value    ${damaged_systems}    Navigation
    List Should Contain Value    ${damaged_systems}    Power
    Log                          Critical systems require repair

2. Configuration Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Required Config Keys
    &{config}          Create Dictionary
    ...                api_key=12345
    ...                timeout=60
    ...                retries=3
    ...                debug=True

    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    api_key
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    timeout
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    retries
    Log                              All required config keys present

3. Error Code Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Expected Errors Present
    @{error_codes}     Create List    ERR-HULL    ERR-POWER    ERR-NAV

    List Should Contain Value    ${error_codes}    ERR-HULL
    List Should Contain Value    ${error_codes}    ERR-POWER
    Log                          Expected error codes detected

4. System Status Verification

*** Test Cases ***
Status Dictionary Validation
    &{systems}         Create Dictionary
    ...                Navigation=OFFLINE
    ...                Power=CRITICAL
    ...                Life_Support=OK
    ...                Communications=DEGRADED

    # Verify all expected systems are tracked
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${systems}    Navigation
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${systems}    Power
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${systems}    Life_Support
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${systems}    Communications

    # Verify critical status exists
    Dictionary Should Contain Value    ${systems}    CRITICAL
    Log                                System status complete

Error Messages

When collection assertions fail, you get specific error messages:

*** Test Cases ***
Failed List Check
    @{systems}         Create List    Navigation    Power

    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    Sensors
    # ❌ ERROR: ['Navigation', 'Power'] does not contain value 'Sensors'
*** Test Cases ***
Failed Dictionary Check
    &{status}          Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE

    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Power
    # ❌ ERROR: Dictionary does not contain key 'Power'

Custom Error Messages

Add custom messages for clarity:

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Messages
    @{systems}         Create List    Navigation    Power
    &{config}          Create Dictionary    timeout=30

    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    Sensors
    ...                          msg=Sensors system not found in damaged list!

    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    api_key
    ...                              msg=Missing required api_key in configuration!

Case Sensitivity

⚠️ Collection assertions are case-sensitive:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Sensitivity
    @{systems}         Create List    Navigation    Power

    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    Navigation    # ✅ PASSES
    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    navigation    # ❌ FAILS - different case!

    &{status}          Create Dictionary    Power=CRITICAL

    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    Power       # ✅ PASSES
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${status}    power       # ❌ FAILS - different case!

Combining with Other Keywords

Collection assertions work great with other validation keywords:

*** Test Cases ***
Complete Collection Validation
    @{systems}         Create List    Navigation    Power    Sensors

    # Check length first
    Length Should Be               ${systems}    3

    # Verify specific items
    List Should Contain Value      ${systems}    Navigation
    List Should Contain Value      ${systems}    Power

    # Ensure it's not empty
    Should Not Be Empty            ${systems}

    Log                            All validations passed

Multiple Membership Checks

*** Test Cases ***
Multiple Item Validation
    @{required_tools}    Create List    Wrench    Welder    Scanner

    # All must be present
    List Should Contain Value    ${required_tools}    Wrench
    List Should Contain Value    ${required_tools}    Welder
    List Should Contain Value    ${required_tools}    Scanner

    Log                          All required tools available

Dictionary Key-Value Pair Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Exact Configuration Match
    &{settings}        Create Dictionary
    ...                max_temp=100
    ...                min_temp=0
    ...                alert_enabled=True

    # Check keys exist
    Dictionary Should Contain Key      ${settings}    max_temp
    Dictionary Should Contain Key      ${settings}    min_temp

    # Check exact key-value pairs
    Dictionary Should Contain Item     ${settings}    max_temp         100
    Dictionary Should Contain Item     ${settings}    alert_enabled    True

    Log                                Configuration validated

Advanced: Nested Collections

Collections can contain other collections:

*** Test Cases ***
Nested Collection Validation
    @{nav_errors}      Create List    ERR-NAV-001    ERR-NAV-002
    @{power_errors}    Create List    ERR-PWR-001

    &{system_errors}   Create Dictionary
    ...                Navigation=${nav_errors}
    ...                Power=${power_errors}

    # Validate outer dictionary
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${system_errors}    Navigation
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${system_errors}    Power

    # Validate inner lists
    ${nav_list}        Get From Dictionary    ${system_errors}    Navigation
    List Should Contain Value    ${nav_list}    ERR-NAV-001

Best Practices

1. Validate Before Accessing

*** Test Cases ***
Safe Access Pattern
    &{config}          Create Dictionary    timeout=30

    # ✅ Good: Validate key exists first
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    timeout
    ${timeout}         Get From Dictionary    ${config}    timeout

    # ❌ Risky: Direct access without validation
    ${value}           Get From Dictionary    ${config}    missing_key    # May fail!

2. Use Specific Collection Keywords

*** Test Cases ***
Specific vs Generic
    @{systems}         Create List    Navigation    Power

    # ✅ Good: Use collection-specific keyword
    List Should Contain Value    ${systems}    Navigation

    # ❌ Less clear: Using generic Should Contain
    Should Contain     ${systems}    Navigation    # Works but less specific

3. Validate Critical Keys

*** Test Cases ***
Critical Configuration
    &{config}          Create Dictionary    api_key=123    timeout=60

    # Validate all critical keys are present
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    api_key
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    timeout
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    endpoint    # ❌ Will fail if missing

    Log                              Configuration complete

Summary: Collection Keywords

KeywordCollection TypeValidates
List Should Contain Value List Value exists in list
Dictionary Should Contain Key Dictionary Key exists in dictionary
Dictionary Should Contain Value Dictionary Value exists in dictionary
Dictionary Should Contain Item Dictionary Exact key-value pair exists

Common Patterns

PatternUse CaseExample
List membership Verify item in collection Is "Navigation" damaged?
Dictionary key check Ensure config setting exists Does config have "timeout"?
Dictionary value check Verify value present Is any system "OFFLINE"?
Key-value pair check Exact config validation Is timeout=30?

Integration with Get Keywords

Combine assertions with retrieval keywords:

*** Test Cases ***
Validate Then Retrieve
    &{systems}         Create Dictionary    Navigation=OFFLINE    Power=CRITICAL

    # First validate key exists
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${systems}    Navigation

    # Then safely retrieve value
    ${nav_status}      Get From Dictionary    ${systems}    Navigation

    # Validate the retrieved value
    Should Be Equal    ${nav_status}    OFFLINE
